# Adjudication Task — Chapter 367

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃367화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|이미 전조(前兆)는 있었다.
  6|
  7|이유도 충분했다.
  8|
  9|구구구구궁!
 10|
 11|지반이 갈라지고 천장이 흔들린다. 지난 수백 년간 사천당문의 어둠을 상징했던 지하 뇌옥이, 잇따른 전투의 여파를 이기지 못하고 붕괴하고 있었다.
 12|
 13|지금껏 뇌옥에서 죽어 간 수많은 죄수들의 원혼, 그리고 아직 멀쩡히 살아 있는 세 사람과 함께.
 14|
 15|“……이런 개 같은 경우를 봤나.”
 16|
 17|적천강은 어이없다는 듯한 표정으로 주위를 둘러보았다.
 18|
 19|분명히 눈을 감기 전에는 숲이었는데, 눈을 뜨니 감옥인지 뭔지 모를 동굴이었다.
 20|
 21|그뿐인가. 아직 성치도 않은 노구를 이끌고 정체도 모르는 웬 썅노무 새끼와 죽자사자 싸우기까지 했다.
 22|
 23|그래. 여기까지는 어느 정도 이해한다. 전투가 끝나자마자 진태경이 혼절한 것? 그것 역시 충분히 있을 수 있는 일이다. 하지만…….
 24|
 25|“아니, 이건 너무한 것 아니냐고. 씨팔.”
 26|
 27|절로 쌍욕이 튀어나오는 상황.
 28|
 29|여긴 어디인가. 노부는 누구인가. 왜 땅이 갈라지고 머리 위로 사람만 한 바위가 쏟아져 내리는가.
 30|
 31|순간 깊은 회한에 사로잡힌 적천강은 하마터면 우화등선할 뻔했다.
 32|
 33|“옘병할.”
 34|
 35|당최 상황이 어찌 되어 가는지는 모르나 우선은 몸부터 피하고 봐야 했다.
 36|
 37|일단 생각이 바로 서자 이어지는 움직임은 전광석화처럼 빨랐다.
 38|
 39|‘우선 태경이 녀석부터 챙기고…… 그런데 이 늙은이는 당최 누구지?’
 40|
 41|에라, 모르겠다.
 42|
 43|혼절한 진태경과 신의를 들쳐 멘 적천강이 황급히 신형을 쏘았다.
 44|
 45|쐐애애액! 쿠웅!
 46|
 47|천장에서 떨어진 거대한 암석이 아슬아슬하게 적천강을 스치며 지면을 박살 냈다. 그러나 그것은 시작에 불과했다.
 48|
 49|쿵! 쿵! 쿠구궁!
 50|
 51|발을 뻗을 때마다 소나기처럼 쏟아지는 기암괴석(奇巖怪石)들의 향연에, 적천강은 모골이 송연해졌다.
 52|
 53|‘잘못하면 이곳에서 뼈를 묻을 수도 있겠구나.’
 54|
 55|척 보아하니 결코 작은 동굴이 아니다.
 56|
 57|만약 수천만 근의 무게를 지닌 절벽이 그들의 머리 위로 내려앉는다면…… 설령 적천강이라고 해도 목숨을 장담할 수 없었다.
 58|
 59|지금처럼 부상의 후유증이 남아 있는 경우에는 더더욱.
 60|
 61|“큭.”
 62|
 63|쩍쩍 갈라진 지면을 밟으며 쏘아지던 신형이 휘청였다. 적천강은 목구멍을 타고 올라오는 핏물을 삼키며 쓰게 웃었다.
 64|
 65|‘꼴이 말이 아니군.’
 66|
 67|오랫동안 움직이지 못한 탓에 돌처럼 뻣뻣한 사지. 극심한 허기와 탈력감이 느껴진다.
 68|
 69|이런 상태에서 어디서 굴러먹다 왔는지도 모르는 웬 괴물 같은 놈과 손을 섞었으니 몸 상태가 더욱 망가지는 건 당연했다. 공력마저 없었다면 진작 쓰러지고도 남았으리라.
 70|
 71|쿠구구궁!
 72|
 73|그 순간, 더욱 크고 거세지는 진동에 적천강은 이를 악물었다.
 74|
 75|‘오냐, 알았으니 재촉하지 말거라. 내 어떻게든 빠져나갈 테니.’
 76|
 77|그에게는 살려야 할 사람이 있었다. 춥고 어두운 기억을 헤매던 그때, 빛과 온기가 되어 준 하나뿐인 제자.
 78|
 79|‘그래, 노부의 하나뿐인 제자지. 제자이고말고.’
 80|
 81|두 사람을 잡은 손에 힘이 들어간다. 몸속 깊숙한 어딘가에서 정체 모를 기운이 솟구치는 듯했다.
 82|
 83|염화일로(炎火一路).
 84|
 85|잠시 주춤했던 적천강의 신형은 한 줄기의 불꽃이 되어 쏘아졌다.
 86|
 87|쉬이이이익!
 88|
 89|앞서 있었던 진태경과 서천마군의 격돌은 지하 뇌옥의 붕괴를 초래했으나, 오히려 적천강에게는 도움이 되었다.
 90|
 91|격돌의 여파로 초토화된 내부. 미로처럼 막혀 있던 벽들이 모조리 무너진 지하 뇌옥은 이제 하나의 거대한 동공에 불과했다.
 92|
 93|‘저쪽이다!’
 94|
 95|신법을 발휘하여 달려나가던 적천강의 눈동자가 번쩍 빛을 발했다.
 96|
 97|어느 곳이든 출입구는 있기 마련.
 98|
 99|어디선가 미약하게 불어오는 바람을 느낀 적천강이 바라본 곳에는, 한 사람이 간신히 드나들 법한 지하 뇌옥의 입구가 있었다.
100|
101|‘어서, 어서……!’
102|
103|적천강은 있는 힘을 다해 신형을 날렸다.
104|
105|뒤집히는 지반을 밟았고, 머리 위로 떨어지는 암석을 피했다.
106|
107|평온한 미소를 띤 채 잠든 것처럼 죽어 있는 노인, 천력마의 시신을 지나쳐 더 멀리, 더 빠르게 쏘아졌다.
108|
109|짧지만 억겁과도 같은 시간 속, 마침내 적천강이 뇌옥의 입구를 향해 마지막 한 걸음을 떼려던 그때였다.
110|
111|“됐……!”
112|
113|드드드득! 구구구궁!
114|
115|지금까지 들려온 모든 굉음을 합친 것만큼, 아니 그 이상의 진동과 굉음. 그와 동시에 천장이 주저앉았다.
116|
117|수백, 수천 년간 축적된 거대한 암석이 뇌옥의 입구를 짓눌렀다.
118|
119|그리고 다음 순간.
120|
121|“썩 비키지 못할까!”
122|
123|지하 뇌옥을 떨어 울리는 창룡후(蒼龍吼)와 함께, 청백의 화염을 머금은 적천강의 일권이 암석의 중앙에 틀어박혔다.
124|
125|꽈아아아앙!
126|
127|멸염신권(滅炎神拳)에 실린 초고온의 열기가 암석을 부수고 녹인다.
128|
129|하늘이 쪼개지는 듯한 굉음 뒤, 느닷없이 들이닥친 열풍이 지하 뇌옥을 휩쓸었다.
130|
131|
132|
133|* * *
134|
135|
136|
137|“이게 무슨.”
138|
139|굉음을 듣고 황급히 달려온 장년의 흑의인은 눈앞에서 벌어지는 광경에 침음성을 삼켰다.
140|
141|콰아아아-!
142|
143|대자연의 붕괴. 사천당문의 뒤를 감싸고 있던 수백 장 높이의 절벽이 천천히 주저앉고 있었다.
144|
145|백여 장 떨어진 이곳에서 지켜보는 것만으로도 경악스럽기 짝이 없는 광경인데, 더욱 큰 문제는 따로 있었다.
146|
147|“부, 부단주. 저곳은 마군께서 계신…….”
148|
149|지하 뇌옥!
150|
151|장년의 흑의인, 암천의 부단주는 수하의 말에 등골이 오싹해졌다.
152|
153|서천마군. 만약 그의 신변에 무슨 문제라도 생긴다면…….
154|
155|‘전부 끝장이다.’
156|
157|이마에서 식은땀이 또르륵 굴러떨어졌다. 사천당문 놈들이 진천뢰를 사용했을 때조차도 이렇게 긴장되지는 않았다.
158|
159|그는 다급한 목소리로 명령을 내렸다.
160|
161|“지금 즉시 흩어져 있는 형제들을 모두 불러 모아라!”
162|
163|“모, 모두 말입니까? 하지만 아직 당문 놈들이 남아 있…….”
164|
165|“그깟 놈들이 문제가 아니다. 어서!”
166|
167|“조, 존명!”
168|
169|바짝 얼어붙은 수하가 품에서 폭죽을 꺼내 당겼다. 펑, 하는 소리와 함께 붉은 빛줄기가 허공에서 터졌다.
170|
171|비상을 알리는 신호에 사천당문 곳곳에 흩어져 있던 흑의인들이 속속 모여들기 시작했다.
172|
173|일백을 훌쩍 넘는 무리가 집결한 것은 불과 촌각이 지난 후였다.
174|
175|“부단주. 명령을 내려 주십시오.”
176|
177|부단주는 방금 말한 놈의 골통을 부숴 버리고 싶었다. 비상을 알렸음에도 머리카락 하나 비추지 않는 단주, 일괴(一怪)도 마찬가지였다.
178|
179|‘빌어먹을.’
180|
181|아직도 붕괴가 진행 중인 절벽을 바라보는 부단주의 목울대가 크게 일렁였다.
182|
183|지금부터 그가 내릴 명령은 자결이나 다름없었다. 무너지는 절벽 아래로 걸어 들어가 서천마군을 찾으라는 것이니까.
184|
185|하지만 다른 선택지는 없다. 명령을 내려야 한다.
186|
187|“저 안에 마군께서 계신다. 부단주인 내가 앞장설 터이니 단 한 사람도 빠짐없이…….”
188|
189|부단주가 힘겹게 명령을 이어 가던 찰나.
190|
191|콰아앙!
192|
193|정체를 알 수 없는 굉음과 함께, 작은 동산을 이루고 있던 암석이 폭발하듯 터져 나갔다.
194|
195|그와 동시에 부단주를 비롯한 모두는 볼 수 있었다. 암석을 뚫고 솟구친 커다란 인영을.
196|
197|“마군! 마군께서 나오셨……!”
198|
199|누군가의 외침은 이어지지 못한 채 흩어졌다.
200|
201|촤악! 파파파팍!
202|
203|마치 포탄처럼 절벽으로부터 한참을 튕겨 나간 인영은 흙탕물과 진흙 위를 구른 끝에 멈췄다.
204|
205|양 옆구리에 제 덩치보다 큰 사람 둘을 단단히 붙들어 맨 노인. 적천강은 먹구름이 가득한 하늘을 바라보며 참았던 숨을 한껏 들이켰다.
206|
207|“푸하아아!”
208|
209|코와 입을 통해 신선한 공기와 빗물이 스며든다.
210|
211|영혼마저 씻겨 내려가는 듯한 상쾌함. 이미 공력은 고갈되었고 몸은 부서질 듯이 아팠지만, 적천강은 진태경을 구해 냈다는 안도감을 느끼며 웃었다.
212|
213|그리고 다음 순간, 비틀거리며 상반신을 일으킨 그는 그대로 굳어 버렸다.
214|
215|“……!”
216|
217|불과 이십여 장 밖, 우뚝 선 채 그를 바라보고 있는 일단의 무리가 있었다.
218|
219|일백이 훌쩍 넘어가는 머릿수에, 손에는 피 묻은 병장기를 들고 있는 흑의인들.
220|
221|적천강이 신음처럼 중얼거렸다.
222|
223|“……염병할. 아무리 봐도 좋은 놈들 같아 보이지는 않는데.”
224|
225|그의 짐작을 확신으로 바꿔 주는 대답이 들려왔다.
226|
227|“암천(暗天)이라 하더군요.”
228|
229|느닷없이 등 뒤에서 들려온 목소리에도 적천강은 놀라지 않았다.
230|
231|지금까지 산전수전을 다 겪은 데다가 지금 막 압살(壓殺)의 위기마저 벗어난 그였다. 달라진 호흡을 통해 자신이 구한 이름 모를 노인이 깨어났다는 것 정도는 알고 있었다.
232|
233|“그렇군. 암천, 그 썅노무 새끼들일 줄 알았지.”
234|
235|욕설을 중얼거린 적천강이 뒤도 돌아보지 않고 말을 이었다.
236|
237|“이곳이 어디인지 알고 있나?”
238|
239|“사천당문입니다. 애석하게도 이미 승부가 난 듯하군요.”
240|
241|“……환장하겠군.”
242|
243|적천강은 짧은 한마디로 소감을 끝맺었다.
244|
245|어떻게 이런 일이 벌어졌는가를 생각할 만큼, 현재 그에게 주어진 시간은 많지 않았다.
246|
247|“이름이 뭐지?”
248|
249|“동봉. 동봉이라 합니다.”
250|
251|“별호는?”
252|
253|“무인이 아니니 별호가 있을 리 없지요.”
254|
255|“단전이 망가졌던데. 무인이 아니다?”
256|
257|“스승님의 성화에 못 이겨 익힌 작은 공부일 뿐. 제가 뜻을 둔 것은 의술이었습니다.”
258|
259|적천강의 눈썹이 꿈틀거렸다.
260|
261|큰 부상을 입었는데도 현기(賢氣)마저 느껴지는 침착한 태도와 말투. 문득 의술이 신의 경지에 다다랐다는 한 의원이 생각나는 것은 왜일까.
262|
263|“신의?”
264|
265|“그저 보잘것없는 늙은 의생일 뿐입니다.”
266|
267|신의의 대답에 적천강이 실소를 흘렸다. 이제야 어찌 된 일인지 알 것 같았다.
268|
269|“고맙네. 다 죽어 가던 늙은이를 깨워 줘서.”
270|
271|“스스로 일어나신 겁니다. 적 대협의 의지가 그만큼 강했던 것이지요.”
272|
273|“어쩔 수 없었지. 웬 천둥벌거숭이 같은 녀석 때문에 잠에서 깼거든.”
274|
275|“바로 그 천둥벌거숭이가 중원을 가로질러 저를 찾아와 부탁했습니다. 적 대협을 살릴 수 있다면 무엇이든지 하겠다고요.”
276|
277|적천강은 옆을 향해 고개를 돌렸다. 피와 진흙으로 범벅이 된 채 쓰러져 있는 진태경의 모습이 그의 눈동자에 담겼다.
278|
279|“……멍청한 녀석 같으니.”
280|
281|지금 저 아이를 깨울 수만 있다면, 깨우고 싶다.
282|

*Hurry. Hurry…!*

[P56]
“Made…!”

[P57]
Rrrrumble! Krrrrrumble!

[P58]

[P59]
The ceiling collapsed.

[P60]

[P61]
Then—

[P62]
“Get the hell out of my way!”

[P63]

[P64]
KWAAAANG!

[P65]
The tremendous heat of the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist shattered and melted the rocks.

[P66]
A roar like the sky splitting apart thundered through the cavern, followed by a sudden blast of scorching wind that swept across the underground prison.

[P67]
* * *

[P68]
“What in the world…?”

[P69]
The middle-aged man in black who had hurried over after hearing the roar swallowed a groan at the sight before him.

[P70]
Rrrrrumble!

[P71]
Nature itself was collapsing. The cliff hundreds of zhang tall that loomed behind the Sichuan Tang Clan was slowly sinking into the earth.

[P72]
The sight was staggering even from more than a hundred zhang away, but there was a far greater problem.

[P73]
“D-Deputy Captain. That’s where the Demon Lord is…”

[P74]
The underground prison!

[P75]
A chill ran down the spine of Dark Heaven’s deputy captain.

[P76]
The Western Heaven Demon Lord. If anything had happened to him…

[P77]
*We’re all finished.*

[P78]
Cold sweat rolled down his forehead. He had not been this nervous even when the Sichuan Tang Clan used Heaven-Shaking Thunder.

[P79]
He barked an urgent order.

[P80]
“Gather every brother scattered across the grounds immediately!”

[P81]
“E-Everyone? But there are still Tang Clan bastards—”

[P82]
“They’re not the problem. Hurry!”

[P83]
“Y-Yes, sir!”

[P84]
The terrified subordinate pulled a signal flare from inside his clothes and triggered it. With a pop, a streak of red light burst across the sky.

[P85]
At the emergency signal, the black-clad men scattered throughout the Sichuan Tang Clan began converging on the area.

[P86]
Within moments, well over a hundred had assembled.

[P87]
“Deputy Captain. Give us your orders.”

[P88]

[P89]
*Damn it.*

[P90]
The deputy captain’s throat bobbed as he stared at the still-collapsing cliff.

[P91]
The order he was about to give was tantamount to suicide. He was going to send them beneath a collapsing cliff to search for the Western Heaven Demon Lord.

[P92]
But there was no other choice. He had to give the order.

[P93]
“The Demon Lord is in there. As deputy captain, I will lead the way, and every last one of you will—”

[P94]
Just as he struggled to finish—

[P95]
KABOOM!

[P96]
An unidentifiable roar erupted, and the pile of rocks forming a small hill exploded outward.

[P97]
The deputy captain and everyone around him saw a large figure burst up through the rubble.

[P98]
“Demon Lord! The Demon Lord has emerged—!”

[P99]
The shout cut off unfinished.

[P100]
Crash! Thud-thud-thud!

[P103]
“Phaaah!”

“…!”

Jeok Cheongang groaned under his breath.

A voice behind him confirmed his suspicion.

“I see. Dark Heaven. I knew it had to be those sons of bitches.”

“Do you know where we are?”

[P121]
“…This is driving me insane.”

“What’s your name?”

“Dong Feng. My name is Dong Feng.”

[P126]
“Your sobriquet?”

[P127]
“I am not a martial artist, so naturally I have none.”

[P128]
“Your dantian was destroyed, yet you claim you aren’t a martial artist?”

[P129]
“I only learned a little because my Master would not stop pestering me. Medicine was always where my heart lay.”

[P130]
Jeok Cheongang’s eyebrow twitched.

[P131]

[P132]
“The Divine Physician?”

[P133]
“I am merely an old medical apprentice of no consequence.”

[P134]

[P135]
“Thank you for waking an old man who was at death’s door.”

[P136]
“You awakened on your own. Your will was simply that strong, Sir Jeok.”

[P137]
“I had no choice. Some reckless fool woke me up.”

[P138]
“That very reckless fool crossed the Central Plains to find me and begged for my help. He said he would do anything if it meant saving you, Sir Jeok.”

[P139]
Jeok Cheongang turned his head. Jin Taekyung lay collapsed beside him, covered in blood and mud.

[P140]
“…What a foolish boy.”

[P141]
If he could wake the boy now, he would.

[P142]
Perhaps then they could have one final conversation.

[P143]
But Jin Taekyung had exhausted every last ounce of strength. He would not awaken. Jeok Cheongang knew that even without the Divine Physician telling him.

[P144]
*Yes. Perhaps… this is better.*

[P145]
Jeok Cheongang slowly rose to his feet. Ignoring the pain stabbing through his entire body, he addressed the Divine Physician behind him.

[P146]
“Still have any strength left?”

[P147]
“I did in my younger days. Before meeting my Master, I worked as a carpenter.”

[P148]
“That’s an unusual past for the Divine Physician. What about now?”

[P149]
“I am seventy years old.”

[P150]
“Your dantian is damaged, so it won’t be easy, but squeeze out every last bit of strength you have. Run as far away as you can.”

[P151]
“With Young Master Jin?”

[P152]
“I’m glad you understand.”

[P153]
After a brief silence, the Divine Physician spoke.

[P154]
“Sir Jeok… You intend to throw your life away.”

[P155]
“Throw it away?”

[P156]
A faint smile touched the corner of Jeok Cheongang’s mouth. His gaze settled on the approaching men in black.

[P157]
“Do you know why a flame dies?”

[P158]
Jeok Cheongang did not wait for an answer.

[P159]
Muddy water splashed beneath his advancing feet. At some point, the rain that had seemed as if it would never end had stopped.

[P160]
His voice rang out, clear and unburdened.

[P161]
“Because it has nothing left to burn. So it slowly dies among the ashes.”

[P162]
Jeok Cheongang was ready to kindle his final flame.

[P163]
He felt neither fear nor anger at the death striding toward him.

[P164]
Only regret.

[P165]
He would no longer be able to remain by his Disciple’s side.

[P166]
“Take care of Taekyung for me.”

[P167]
Just as Jeok Cheongang stepped forward after making that heartfelt request, the Divine Physician spoke.

[P168]
“After witnessing countless births, aging, sickness, and deaths, I began to wonder. Does the underworld truly exist? If so, who is this fellow called Yama? And if I go there, will I meet the patients I failed to save?”

[P169]
“…?”

[P170]
“Whenever such questions troubled me, my Master would say, ‘The underworld must be full from all the people you sent ahead of you. You should ascend to the celestial realm instead and keep the immortals company.’”

[P171]
The Divine Physician looked at Jeok Cheongang and continued quietly.

[P172]
“Sir Jeok. The underworld is full. Please wait a little longer.”

[P173]
“…!”

[P174]
Every hair on Jeok Cheongang’s body stood on end. His head snapped up.

[P175]
High above, bathed in sunlight streaming between the retreating dark clouds, stood a boy.

[P176]
*No. Not a boy. That man is…!*

[P177]
His eyes were clear and bright like a boy’s, yet ancient and seasoned, devoid of the slightest emotion.

[P178]
Jeok Cheongang had seen those eyes only once, a very long time ago.

[P179]
That was precisely why he could never forget the feeling they evoked.

[P180]
The boy’s appearance brought someone to mind, and Jeok Cheongang cried out in shock.

[P181]
“The Slaughter Saint…!”

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.

- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.

- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 367

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃367화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|이미 전조(前兆)는 있었다.
  6|
  7|이유도 충분했다.
  8|
  9|구구구구궁!
 10|
 11|지반이 갈라지고 천장이 흔들린다. 지난 수백 년간 사천당문의 어둠을 상징했던 지하 뇌옥이, 잇따른 전투의 여파를 이기지 못하고 붕괴하고 있었다.
 12|
 13|지금껏 뇌옥에서 죽어 간 수많은 죄수들의 원혼, 그리고 아직 멀쩡히 살아 있는 세 사람과 함께.
 14|
 15|“……이런 개 같은 경우를 봤나.”
 16|
 17|적천강은 어이없다는 듯한 표정으로 주위를 둘러보았다.
 18|
 19|분명히 눈을 감기 전에는 숲이었는데, 눈을 뜨니 감옥인지 뭔지 모를 동굴이었다.
 20|
 21|그뿐인가. 아직 성치도 않은 노구를 이끌고 정체도 모르는 웬 썅노무 새끼와 죽자사자 싸우기까지 했다.
 22|
 23|그래. 여기까지는 어느 정도 이해한다. 전투가 끝나자마자 진태경이 혼절한 것? 그것 역시 충분히 있을 수 있는 일이다. 하지만…….
 24|
 25|“아니, 이건 너무한 것 아니냐고. 씨팔.”
 26|
 27|절로 쌍욕이 튀어나오는 상황.
 28|
 29|여긴 어디인가. 노부는 누구인가. 왜 땅이 갈라지고 머리 위로 사람만 한 바위가 쏟아져 내리는가.
 30|
 31|순간 깊은 회한에 사로잡힌 적천강은 하마터면 우화등선할 뻔했다.
 32|
 33|“옘병할.”
 34|
 35|당최 상황이 어찌 되어 가는지는 모르나 우선은 몸부터 피하고 봐야 했다.
 36|
 37|일단 생각이 바로 서자 이어지는 움직임은 전광석화처럼 빨랐다.
 38|
 39|‘우선 태경이 녀석부터 챙기고…… 그런데 이 늙은이는 당최 누구지?’
 40|
 41|에라, 모르겠다.
 42|
 43|혼절한 진태경과 신의를 들쳐 멘 적천강이 황급히 신형을 쏘았다.
 44|
 45|쐐애애액! 쿠웅!
 46|
 47|천장에서 떨어진 거대한 암석이 아슬아슬하게 적천강을 스치며 지면을 박살 냈다. 그러나 그것은 시작에 불과했다.
 48|
 49|쿵! 쿵! 쿠구궁!
 50|
 51|발을 뻗을 때마다 소나기처럼 쏟아지는 기암괴석(奇巖怪石)들의 향연에, 적천강은 모골이 송연해졌다.
 52|
 53|‘잘못하면 이곳에서 뼈를 묻을 수도 있겠구나.’
 54|
 55|척 보아하니 결코 작은 동굴이 아니다.
 56|
 57|만약 수천만 근의 무게를 지닌 절벽이 그들의 머리 위로 내려앉는다면…… 설령 적천강이라고 해도 목숨을 장담할 수 없었다.
 58|
 59|지금처럼 부상의 후유증이 남아 있는 경우에는 더더욱.
 60|
 61|“큭.”
 62|
 63|쩍쩍 갈라진 지면을 밟으며 쏘아지던 신형이 휘청였다. 적천강은 목구멍을 타고 올라오는 핏물을 삼키며 쓰게 웃었다.
 64|
 65|‘꼴이 말이 아니군.’
 66|
 67|오랫동안 움직이지 못한 탓에 돌처럼 뻣뻣한 사지. 극심한 허기와 탈력감이 느껴진다.
 68|
 69|이런 상태에서 어디서 굴러먹다 왔는지도 모르는 웬 괴물 같은 놈과 손을 섞었으니 몸 상태가 더욱 망가지는 건 당연했다. 공력마저 없었다면 진작 쓰러지고도 남았으리라.
 70|
 71|쿠구구궁!
 72|
 73|그 순간, 더욱 크고 거세지는 진동에 적천강은 이를 악물었다.
 74|
 75|‘오냐, 알았으니 재촉하지 말거라. 내 어떻게든 빠져나갈 테니.’
 76|
 77|그에게는 살려야 할 사람이 있었다. 춥고 어두운 기억을 헤매던 그때, 빛과 온기가 되어 준 하나뿐인 제자.
 78|
 79|‘그래, 노부의 하나뿐인 제자지. 제자이고말고.’
 80|
 81|두 사람을 잡은 손에 힘이 들어간다. 몸속 깊숙한 어딘가에서 정체 모를 기운이 솟구치는 듯했다.
 82|

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
